Now that we're firmly in the Apple Silicon era, virtualization on macOS has become very robust. Parallels Desktop 27 takes it a step further with an all-new Metal graphics driver, bringing OpenGL 4.3 support to Windows virtual machines on Apple Silicon, faster local AI workloads, and a suite of enterprise features designed for IT teams to manage and deploy Windows on macOS. Here's my review of the new features after using it.

About Apple @ Work: Bradley Chambers has been managing Apple IT since 2009. Through his experience deploying and managing firewalls, switches, mobile device management systems, enterprise-grade Wi-Fi, and thousands of Macs and iPads, Bradley will share how Apple IT managers deploy Apple devices, build networks to support them, train users, share stories from the front lines of IT management, and explore how Apple can improve its products for IT departments.

圖像效能提升

The headlining feature of Parallels Desktop 27 is an all-new Metal graphics driver that brings hardware-accelerated OpenGL 4.3 support to Windows virtual machines on Apple Silicon, which Parallels says is unique among Mac virtualization tools today. OpenGL 4.3 is the minimum graphics specification required by many professional Windows applications. With this boost, apps like ArcGIS Pro, ZWCAD, and Blender 4.3 can now run inside a virtualized environment on macOS.

Parallels claims OpenGL graphics performance gains of up to 160% on M3 and later Macs. In ArcGIS Pro, 3D rendering is up to 35% faster, and overall workflow times are reduced by up to 24%.

The improved OpenGL support isn't just a win for professional engineering software—any program that relies on that graphics technology stack, including games, benefits. I hadn't gamed on a PC in about 20 years, and spending my entire session inside a Windows VM on an M5 Pro while testing Parallels Desktop 27 was a stunning experience.

本地 AI 開發速度提升

Parallels Desktop 27 also adds support for the Scalable Matrix Extension (SME2) instructions on M4 and later Macs in both Linux and Windows virtual machines. According to Parallels, this can deliver up to 7× faster AI and machine learning matrix operations, up to 1.75× faster neural network inference, and improved performance for tools like Ollama and llama.cpp running inside a VM. For developers who want to build and test AI workloads locally rather than burning cloud credits on every prompt, it's a solid upgrade, and another example of Apple Silicon's relevance in the AI era.

IT 方面有什麼新功能？

Parallels Desktop for Enterprise can now determine via the CLI whether an installation was activated with a license key or via SSO, making it easier for organizations using Jamf to build extension attributes around that for device management and reporting.

Alongside Desktop 27, Parallels has also refreshed its SOC 2 compliance certification. Additionally, Secure Golden Images Provisioning now allows approved VM images to be distributed via enterprise storage options, including Azure Blob Storage and SharePoint, with improved declarative deployment for fully configured, zero-touch Windows VMs. For deployments at scale, this is a big deal.

總結

There's a lot to like in Parallels Desktop 27, whether you're an engineer, developer, or gamer. A lot of the ecosystem we live in is cross-platform or web-based, but when you need to run a Windows application on macOS, it's never felt this smooth or this close to native. This is the best version of Parallels Desktop ever, and if you have high-performance Windows applications you need to run on a Mac, it's worth the upgrade. I know some customers don't love the subscription model, but if you need to run virtual machines on macOS, the yearly upgrades are absolutely worth it, as Parallels continuously rolls out development to keep up with Apple's latest features.

Want to see if your Windows applications are compatible with Parallels Desktop? Head over to www.parallels.com/apps and search their database of over 200,000 supported applications.

Parallels Desktop 27 is available now in Standard, Pro, Business, and Enterprise editions.
